fixes.explanation: I get why debt came to mind, because plenty of people feel like they owe somebody. But Paul doesn't say we have debt with God. He says that since we have been justified through faith, "…we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ…"

Distance isn't what Paul says, friend. He says that since we have been justified through faith, we have peace with God. Right after that he says we have "…gained access by faith into this grace in which we stand." So the word Paul uses here is peace.
Hope is the word, baker. Paul says, "And we rejoice in the hope of the glory of God." That comes right after he says we stand in this grace, so we're not rejoicing from shaky ground.

That would be an easier verse to read, wouldn't it? But Paul doesn't say we rejoice in our good deeds. He says, "…we also rejoice in our sufferings, because we know that suffering produces perseverance…" That's his reason, and it keeps going: perseverance, then character, then hope.

That's the reason, baker. Paul says, "…hope does not disappoint us, because God has poured out His love into our hearts…" The hope rests on God's love, and Paul says that love has already been poured out into our hearts.
His prophets is a fair guess, but it's not what Paul says here. He says God poured out His love into our hearts "…through the Holy Spirit, whom He has given us." The Holy Spirit is the answer.

Angels are impressive, and the angel who called me out of that drawer still makes me a little nervous. But Paul doesn't say angels here. He says God poured out His love into our hearts "…through the Holy Spirit, whom He has given us."

True, baker. Paul says, "Therefore, since we have now been justified by His blood, how much more shall we be saved from wrath through Him!" I think Paul is excited here, and I would be too. We've been justified by His blood, and we'll be saved from wrath through Him.

It's actually True. Paul says, "…since we have now been justified by His blood, how much more shall we be saved from wrath through Him!" So the text says we'll be saved from wrath through Him. Justified by His blood now, saved from wrath through Him.

Offerings at the temple is a fair guess, but Paul doesn't name them here. He says, "…when we were enemies of God, we were reconciled to Him through the death of His Son…" The reconciling comes through the Son's death.
Miracles is a fair guess, but Paul doesn't say miracles here. He says, "…how much more, having been reconciled, shall we be saved through His life!" The word he uses is life.
The apostles is a fair guess, but that's not what Paul says. He says, "…we also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ…" The rejoicing is in God.

Angels are impressive, no argument from me. But Paul doesn't say we rejoice in the angels. He says, "…we also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received reconciliation."
